# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

15	### How to read this document
16	
17	The GDDs already fix most of the architecture: each one names its state block, its step hook (divisor, offset, `after:`), its mutators and its read view, and the kernel GDD fixes the tick phases and the write rules. This document does not re-decide any of that. It assembles those contracts into one map, names the layers and boundaries they imply, records the decisions that still belong in ADRs, and lists the conflicts left between GDDs. Where this document and a GDD disagree, the GDD is the source and this document is wrong; raise it with `/propagate-design-change`.

70	## System Layer Map
71	
72	### The layering rule
73	
74	The systems index orders systems by dependency (Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish). The architecture layers below are **responsibility** layers. One test decides the side: **a system that registers a SIM state block or a step hook is simulation; a system that registers none and only subscribes to the kernel is presentation.** Static content that is loaded once and never changes at runtime is data. The kernel and Save/Load are foundation because everything else registers with them.
75	
76	The simulation side never reads the presentation side. Presentation reads committed simulation state through read views and writes only engine-side nodes. The one presentation class that may change the simulation is `INPUT_SURFACE`, and it does so only by submitting commands.

241	## Data Flow
242	
243	### 1. Frame update path
244	
245	One rendered frame. The tick is driven from `_process`, never from the physics callback (kernel CR-1a; see Open Question OQ-1 for three GDDs that still cite the physics callback).
246	
247	```
248	Engine frame (_process order by process_priority)
249	│
250	├─ priority 0  Input Adapter (INPUT_SURFACE)
251	│     read InputMap actions → change-only intents (set_move_intent, set_aim ≤ every 3 ticks)
252	│     → kernel.submit(type, payload, actor, correlation)            [sync call, queued]
253	│
254	├─ priority 1  TickDriver (the only wall-clock reader)
255	│     accumulator += delta_us × TICK_RATE ; ticks = min(floor(acc / 1e6), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME=4)
256	│     boundary service (P6 work deferred from last frame: SAVING / LOADING)
257	│     repeat ticks times: Kernel.step()  ──► P0 Begin
258	│                                           P1 Intake   (queue → this tick's batch, coalesce intents)
259	│                                           P2 Dispatch (authority check → validate → apply in WriteScope)
260	│                                           P3 Step     (hooks whose T mod divisor == offset, topo order)
261	│                                           P4 Commit
262	│                                           P5 Notify   (batches queued; PRESENTATION merged per frame)
263	│                                           P6 Boundary (snapshot/restore/pause requests)
264	│     drop lag (LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0) ; flush results ; compute tick_alpha
265	│
266	└─ priority 2  Presentation subscribers (render callback)
267	      handlers only mark dirty → draw using read views at tick_alpha:
268	      pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) × tick_alpha)
269	      Avatar Presenter → Lighting → Trail → Instruments (perceived()) → HUD (perceived()) → Audio
270	      Pipeline root: CameraSolver → canvas_transform in frame_pre_draw
271	```
272	
273	**P3 hook schedule (MVP).** Divisor and offset decide which ticks a hook runs on; `after:` orders hooks that run on the same tick. An `after:` edge between hooks that do not always coincide must declare `tolerates_stale` (CR-3).
274	
275	| Hook | Owner | Divisor | Offset | After |
276	|---|---|---|---|---|
277	| `controller.step` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `suit.vitals` (stale-tolerant) |
278	| `layout.doors` | Layout | 1 | 0 | — |
279	| `body.integrate` | Body | 1 | 0 | `controller.step`, `layout.doors` |
280	| `controller.noise` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate` |
281	| `emitter.place` | Emitter | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` (stale-tolerant) |
282	| `interaction.step` | Interaction | 1 | 0 | `emitter.place` |
283	| `assembly.step` | Assembly | 1 | 0 | `interaction.step` |
284	| `transit.step` | Web Map | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` |
285	| `graph.propagate.power` | Graph | 6 | 0 | — |
286	| `graph.propagate.atmo` | Graph | 6 | 2 | `graph.propagate.power` (stale-tolerant) |
287	| `graph.propagate.failure` | Graph | 6 | 4 | `graph.propagate.atmo` (stale-tolerant) |
288	| `suit.vitals` | Suit | 6 | 2 | `graph.propagate.atmo` |
289	| `attention.step` | Attention | 6 | 0 | `graph.propagate.power`, `emitter.place` |
290	| `horror.step` | Horror | 5 | 0 | `attention.step`, `emitter.place` |
291	| `sanity.drift` | Sanity | 12 | 0 | `graph.propagate.failure`, `suit.vitals` (stale-tolerant) |
292	
293	The kernel builds this order once in BOOTING; an unknown `after:` id or a cycle fails boot. ADR-0003 records the sort; each owning GDD remains the authority on its own row.
294	
295	**Budgets (P99, release export, RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK):** P3 ≤ 2.0 ms (alarm at `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 ms); frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms for one tick and ≤ 6.0 ms for four; Graph hooks ≤ 0.5 ms on a hook tick; `emitter.place` + exposure ≤ 0.4 ms; Sanity median ≤ 0.5 ms; pipeline `_process` ≤ 0.5 ms; light CPU ≤ 1.0 ms steady; total frame ≤ 14.9 ms desktop and ≤ 30.0 ms Deck (90 % of the 16.6 / 33.3 ms ceilings, ruling R12).

336	### 4. Event and notification path
337	
338	- **Simulation → presentation:** P5 notification `(block_id, tick, change_keys)` with no state payload. Dirty keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id`, namespaced per block. Past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) a batch collapses to `ALL`. PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches are merged across a multi-tick frame and delivered once; INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick.
339	- **Presentation → simulation:** only commands through an INPUT_SURFACE handle. There is no other path.
340	- **Simulation → simulation:** synchronous calls inside the tick: pure reads of another block's read view, and published mutators called inside the caller's WriteScope. A cross-block write is always a published mutator of the owning system (Class A checked or Class B clamped). Simulation code never subscribes to notifications (an object that owns a block or hook never subscribes, CR-10).
341	- **P5 events** (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`, …) are notifications that carry no simulation state; Save/Load reads them as autosave triggers.
342	- **Engine signals** are used only inside presentation (e.g. `card_opened`, settings change). The kernel's observer registry is not built on engine signals (decision for ADR-0004).

344	### 5. Perception path (the one place a lie can enter)
345	
346	```
347	Sanity (SIM) ── sanity.drift ──► sanity.perception (PERCEPTION_OUT, per viewer, never persisted)
348	                                        │  (simulation reads of it return empty + violation)
349	Instrument / HUD presenter ── perceived(ref, viewer) ──► Perception Filter
350	                                        │ reads true value (Graph / Suit read view)
351	                                        │ reads sanity.perception entry for (ref, viewer)
352	                                        ▼
353	                               Perceived {displayed_value, motion_mode, leak_amplitude_pm, …}
354	Truth channels never pass through the Filter: Failure & Trail, true reveal radius (Lighting L0),
355	character sprites, crewmate beams, HUD frame, physical consequences in the Graph.
356	```

358	The Graph's `state_hash` is identical with and without perception content; the simulation never computes a perceived value.

381	   restore each WORLD block in restore_after order (two-phase: decode+validate into scratch, then swap)
382	   post_restore each block in the same order (derived caches, cross-block verification)
383	   rebuild binding table half (b) from binding sources (seat_bindings, beam_bindings)
384	   reproduction check: state_hash vs header (reported, never a fallback reason)
385	   → RUNNING; accumulator cleared; camera CUT; Adapter resends intents; first frame passes through the Filter
386	```
387	
388	**restore_after order (MVP):** `layout.state` → `graph.state` → `body.state` → `controller.state` → `emitter.state`, `suit.state` → `interaction.state` → `assembly.state`, `web.state`; then Attention, Horror and Sanity (their restore_after lists are in their GDDs; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG).
389	
390	**Threading.** Exactly one thread boundary exists in the MVP: the save writer (and its read-back). Everything else, kernel, owner callables and presentation, runs on the main thread; `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden (CR-1a).
391	
392	### 8. Initialisation order
393	
394	```
395	1. Engine boot; project.godot guard rails asserted (stretch, filters, snap, hdr_2d, physics_interpolation off)
396	2. Pipeline root builds the viewport stack (BOOTING → PRESENTING)
397	3. Content data loads in a fixed order: Item DB → section templates (manifest order) → world records,
398	   verb tables, tuning tables; boot lints and invariant assertions (refuse the build on failure)
399	4. Kernel BOOTING: owners register blocks, command types, hooks, binding sources, diagnostics channels
400	   (Layout, Graph last of the Item DB → Layout → Graph chain; then Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit,
401	   Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity). Registration then freezes; hook topo-sort.
402	5. Presentation subscribers subscribe (Lighting, Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, PROJECTORs, Debug)
403	6. Main menu (Chart Table) → New Game: Save/Load new_game(seed) → kernel request_new_game(seed, 0)
404	   → Web Map init_world inside one WriteScope: Layout build_section → Emitter instantiate_section_emitters
405	   → Interaction sync_section → PROJECTOR notification → initial NEW_GAME generation written
406	   or Continue: load path (§ 7)
407	```
408	
409	---
410	
411	## API Boundaries
412	
413	Signatures are GDScript (typed). They restate the GDD contracts at the boundary; the GDD anchor in brackets is the authority.
414	
415	### Kernel ingress and registration [command-simulation-layer CR-4..CR-10, CR-19]
416	
417	```gdscript
418	# Ingress (INPUT_SURFACE handle only). Fire-and-forget: returns nothing, calls nothing.
419	func submit(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, actor: int = NO_ACTOR, correlation: int = 0) -> void
420	# SYSTEM-origin submission from a step hook or apply (dedupe optional).

666	
667	## Architecture Principles
668	
669	1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
670	2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
671	3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
672	4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
673	5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
674	6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

## Architecture Principles

1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

content.thinking:
I'm checking whether the override's return type actually matters here—it only applies if there's a base class, so the contract holds. But I'm flagging that TR-pc-004 and TR-pc-005 are stale, and TR-pc-005's hook order seems to conflict with the hook table since suit.vitals runs after controller.step.

Tracing the dependency chain to check for cycles: controller.step after suit.vitals, suit.vitals after graph.propagate.atmo, graph.propagate.failure, emitter.place after graph.propagate.failure — no cycle found, that's fine, though the stale-tolerant tick offsets look consistent enough.

The weld system faults the entire game on any failed weld with no rollback, which seems feasible for a solo dev but the check-then-apply logic across four systems depends on can_join staying perfectly consistent, so I'd want a property test for that. More concerning is the save worker's synchronous snapshot at P6 taking up to 16.7ms for 32 blocks against a 14.9ms frame budget — that's a real frame hitch risk, and there's also an unresolved concern about rename atomicity being unverified on Windows.

I'm uncertain whether Godot's DirAccess.rename succeeds when the target file already exists on Windows, since I'm not sure if it uses MoveFileEx under the hood — I should flag this as unverified and needing a spike. Threading with FileAccess and HashingContext for re-reading and hashing should be fine since those instances are thread-local.

For the hot path budget, I'm estimating GDScript throughput since I don't have hard numbers — something like tens of millions of simple ops per second, which would put a 2ms budget on Steam Deck at roughly 70k-200k ops across all hooks per tick cycle, but I need to hedge this clearly as a rough estimate rather than a verified fact, and flag that S1 needs to actually measure it. I'm also noting that the graph propagation phase at 0.5ms per hook tick depends on graph size, which I haven't actually read yet.

Other risks worth flagging: how packed arrays are passed in GDScript (reference vs copy-on-write), the warning-ignore syntax requiring 4.2+, int64 literal overflow behavior, and that integer overflow wraps in practice even though right shifts are arithmetic rather than logical, so masking is needed for logical shifts. I also want to note the practical difficulty of enforcing lint rules in GDScript given the lack of a proper AST tooling ecosystem.

Static analysis is genuinely weak here—gdlint exists but is limited, so a custom regex-based EditorScript tool is the realistic path, though enforcing "only this file can write this field" rules via regex is fragile. Project-level warning settings can be bumped to errors for things like untyped declarations and unsafe operations, but GDScript has no real privacy enforcement or interfaces, so I'd rely on base classes and duck typing instead. I also need to flag the cyclic dependency risk between Graph and Layout modules—typed cyclic references work fine with class_name in Godot 4.x, but preload-based cycles will error, so the mandate should be to always use class_name and ban direct preload cycles.

On the completion token contract, I'm realizing GDScript can't statically enforce "must return ctx.complete()"—the kernel needs to check the returned token's identity unconditionally at runtime rather than relying on asserts that get stripped in release builds, though a typed return signature does at least force every code path to return something. There's also ambiguity about whether owner callables are registered as plain Callable objects or as virtual methods on a base class, which changes whether Godot 4.7's typed-override-inheritance rule even applies, and the types referenced in the validate signature—ReadViews, WriteScope, ApplyContext—still need clear definitions.

I'm also flagging missing interface definitions for several structs like BlockDescriptor, ChangeBatch, QueryBuffer, FailureSlice, and the FAULT_CODE enum, plus a tension between using Kernel as a static/global singleton versus the stated coding standard of fully injected dependencies—leaning toward having presentation nodes receive the kernel through an explicit setup call instead. On the allocation side, value types like Vector2i and Rect2i are stack-based with no heap cost, while RefCounted results and Dictionary-based command payloads do allocate, which seems acceptable at low rates but worth keeping in mind for performance-sensitive paths.

I'm digging into whether "zero heap allocation" claims can actually be verified in GDScript—Packed arrays aren't Objects, so OBJECT_COUNT won't catch them, and MEMORY_STATIC deltas are too coarse to prove anything precise. This makes me think the acceptance criteria for zero-allocation requirements like TR-lsg-025 and TR-cmd-032 need to be redefined as a combination of OBJECT_COUNT/MEMORY_STATIC deltas plus a code-review lint banning allocation-triggering syntax in hot files, so the requirement is actually testable rather than aspirational.

I'm also now questioning gdUnit4's compatibility with Godot 4.7 and whether performance benchmarks even can run inside the test framework versus needing a separate exported harness, plus noting that `assert` gets stripped in release builds which breaks a kernel context check. Looking at the ADR structure, some single ADRs cover 60+ requirements each, which is too large to be reviewable, and having 33 ADRs required before coding even starts seems like heavy process overhead for a solo developer.

Doing rough arithmetic on scope — 794 TRs across 26 systems works out to roughly 30 TRs per system, and even at a quarter-day per TR that's close to 200 working days, about ten months full-time before any art or content work begins. That's just illustrative math to flag the scale, not a definitive estimate; the actual scope-cutting decision belongs to a producer or creative director. I'm planning a couple quick verification checks (addon presence, save/load rename handling, current GDScript 4.7 practices) before calling the advisor once, prioritizing those checks first given the budget.

I'm checking whether the override's return type actually matters here—it only applies if there's a base class, so the contract holds. But I'm flagging that TR-pc-004 and TR-pc-005 are stale, and TR-pc-005's hook order seems to conflict with the hook table since suit.vitals runs after controller.step.

Tracing the dependency chain to check for cycles: controller.step after suit.vitals, suit.vitals after graph.propagate.atmo, graph.propagate.failure, emitter.place after graph.propagate.failure — no cycle found, that's fine, though the stale-tolerant tick offsets look consistent enough.

The weld system faults the entire game on any failed weld with no rollback, which seems feasible for a solo dev but the check-then-apply logic across four systems depends on can_join staying perfectly consistent, so I'd want a property test for that. More concerning is the save worker's synchronous snapshot at P6 taking up to 16.7ms for 32 blocks against a 14.9ms frame budget — that's a real frame hitch risk, and there's also an unresolved concern about rename atomicity being unverified on Windows.

I'm uncertain whether Godot's DirAccess.rename succeeds when the target file already exists on Windows, since I'm not sure if it uses MoveFileEx under the hood — I should flag this as unverified and needing a spike. Threading with FileAccess and HashingContext for re-reading and hashing should be fine since those instances are thread-local.

For the hot path budget, I'm estimating GDScript throughput since I don't have hard numbers — something like tens of millions of simple ops per second, which would put a 2ms budget on Steam Deck at roughly 70k-200k ops across all hooks per tick cycle, but I need to hedge this clearly as a rough estimate rather than a verified fact, and flag that S1 needs to actually measure it. I'm also noting that the graph propagation phase at 0.5ms per hook tick depends on graph size, which I haven't actually read yet.

Other risks worth flagging: how packed arrays are passed in GDScript (reference vs copy-on-write), the warning-ignore syntax requiring 4.2+, int64 literal overflow behavior, and that integer overflow wraps in practice even though right shifts are arithmetic rather than logical, so masking is needed for logical shifts. I also want to note the practical difficulty of enforcing lint rules in GDScript given the lack of a proper AST tooling ecosystem.

Static analysis is genuinely weak here—gdlint exists but is limited, so a custom regex-based EditorScript tool is the realistic path, though enforcing "only this file can write this field" rules via regex is fragile. Project-level warning settings can be bumped to errors for things like untyped declarations and unsafe operations, but GDScript has no real privacy enforcement or interfaces, so I'd rely on base classes and duck typing instead. I also need to flag the cyclic dependency risk between Graph and Layout modules—typed cyclic references work fine with class_name in Godot 4.x, but preload-based cycles will error, so the mandate should be to always use class_name and ban direct preload cycles.

On the completion token contract, I'm realizing GDScript can't statically enforce "must return ctx.complete()"—the kernel needs to check the returned token's identity unconditionally at runtime rather than relying on asserts that get stripped in release builds, though a typed return signature does at least force every code path to return something. There's also ambiguity about whether owner callables are registered as plain Callable objects or as virtual methods on a base class, which changes whether Godot 4.7's typed-override-inheritance rule even applies, and the types referenced in the validate signature—ReadViews, WriteScope, ApplyContext—still need clear definitions.

I'm also flagging missing interface definitions for several structs like BlockDescriptor, ChangeBatch, QueryBuffer, FailureSlice, and the FAULT_CODE enum, plus a tension between using Kernel as a static/global singleton versus the stated coding standard of fully injected dependencies—leaning toward having presentation nodes receive the kernel through an explicit setup call instead. On the allocation side, value types like Vector2i and Rect2i are stack-based with no heap cost, while RefCounted results and Dictionary-based command payloads do allocate, which seems acceptable at low rates but worth keeping in mind for performance-sensitive paths.

I'm digging into whether "zero heap allocation" claims can actually be verified in GDScript—Packed arrays aren't Objects, so OBJECT_COUNT won't catch them, and MEMORY_STATIC deltas are too coarse to prove anything precise. This makes me think the acceptance criteria for zero-allocation requirements like TR-lsg-025 and TR-cmd-032 need to be redefined as a combination of OBJECT_COUNT/MEMORY_STATIC deltas plus a code-review lint banning allocation-triggering syntax in hot files, so the requirement is actually testable rather than aspirational.

I'm also now questioning gdUnit4's compatibility with Godot 4.7 and whether performance benchmarks even can run inside the test framework versus needing a separate exported harness, plus noting that `assert` gets stripped in release builds which breaks a kernel context check. Looking at the ADR structure, some single ADRs cover 60+ requirements each, which is too large to be reviewable, and having 33 ADRs required before coding even starts seems like heavy process overhead for a solo developer.

Doing rough arithmetic on scope — 794 TRs across 26 systems works out to roughly 30 TRs per system, and even at a quarter-day per TR that's close to 200 working days, about ten months full-time before any art or content work begins. That's just illustrative math to flag the scale, not a definitive estimate; the actual scope-cutting decision belongs to a producer or creative director. I'm planning a couple quick verification checks (addon presence, save/load rename handling, current GDScript 4.7 practices) before calling the advisor once, prioritizing those checks first given the budget.

The snapshot capture at 16.7ms for 32 blocks exceeds the frame budget of 14.9ms, meaning autosave would cause a one-frame hitch — worth flagging but not blocking. Since gdUnit4 isn't installed yet, I'll go straight to a CONCERNS verdict without routing through the advisor.

## LP-FEASIBILITY: CONCERNS

No blocker makes the architecture unimplementable as written. Nothing in it needs an API that GDScript 4.7.2 lacks. It is a one-programmer project only if the performance claims are measured early and the interface gaps below are closed before the Foundation ADRs are accepted.

I read all of `architecture.md` (headings plus every range) and spot-checked `tr-baseline.md` and `breaking-changes.md`. I did not read the 26 GDDs, so I did not verify per-system sizes such as Graph node counts. The performance reasoning below is therefore from the stated budgets only.

### Basis and limits

- **No ADRs exist**, and `addons/` has no `plugin.cfg`, so gdUnit4 is not installed. Every testability claim is unproven.
- **Budgets are stated but unmeasured.** OQ-10 and spike S1 say so themselves: P3 ≤ 2.0 ms and frame sim ≤ 4.0 ms (1 tick) or ≤ 6.0 ms (4 ticks) at P99 on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. Graph hooks are ≤ 0.5 ms on a hook tick, and `emitter.place` plus exposure is ≤ 0.4 ms.
- **The Deck frame ceiling is 30.0 ms and the desktop one is 14.9 ms.** The worst case (4 catch-up ticks, 6 ms) is 40 % of the desktop frame before rendering. LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0 drops the excess, so a slow tick degrades to slow-motion rather than a spiral. That choice is sound.

### (a) Hard or risky to implement in GDScript

1. **Zero-allocation hot paths cannot be verified.**
   - TR-lsg-025 ("zero heap allocations per phase") and TR-cmd-032 ("0 kernel container allocations") have no direct GDScript measurement.
   - `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` sees RefCounted objects but not Packed or Array buffers. `MEMORY_STATIC` is too coarse.
   - Rewrite these acceptance criteria as an OBJECT_COUNT delta plus a static-scan lint over the hot files. The lint bans `[]`, `{}`, `.duplicate()`, `Packed*Array()` constructors and `Dictionary` payloads. Otherwise the AC is unfalsifiable.
   - Alternatives that fit: a per-file "hot" marker that the lint keys off, or a canary test asserting OBJECT_COUNT is flat over N ticks.

2. **Integer SoA performance is plausible but the evidence is missing.**
   - Typed local indexing of `PackedInt32Array`/`PackedInt64Array` has a fast path, but each cross-system accessor call and each `Callable.call` costs far more than the arithmetic around it.
   - Budgets that count accessor calls (`compartment_p(cid)`, `lit(ref)`, `rects_in`) will be dominated by call overhead, not data layout. Spike S1 should measure calls per ms, not only loop arithmetic.
   - GDExtension for the Graph is already named as rung 3, VS-A only. Keep it as the escape hatch, and note it breaks "GDScript only".

3. **Integer-overflow hashing (H64 and mix64) has two hazards.**
   - `>>` is arithmetic in GDScript, so logical shifts need masking.
   - Hex literals above INT64_MAX do not parse. S0-b covers the literal; add the shift behaviour to the same spike.
   - The hash spec itself is ambiguous (OQ-8). Golden vectors must exist before ADR-0005 is Accepted, not after.

4. **Typed-return override rule is likely a mislabel.** The 4.7 rule applies to overrides of a base-class method. The owner callables look like registered `Callable`s on `RefCounted` owners, not overrides.
   - The doc must say which it is: a virtual-method base class (`BlockOwner`) or free Callables.
   - If Callables, the 4.7 note is moot and the real enforcement is simpler: GDScript already rejects a typed function with a path that has no return.
   - KRN-CTX-06's "assert stripped on release" concern then reduces to one rule: the kernel must verify the returned token identity with a real `if`, never an `assert`.

5. **Cyclic typed references between systems.** The dependency diagram shows Layout and Graph depending on each other (Layout consumes Graph `instantiate_section`; Graph consumes Layout room identity). Assembly, Interaction and Body also form loops.
   - GDScript tolerates cycles through `class_name`, but `preload` cycles fail to parse.
   - Mandate `class_name` plus typed interface base classes (`GraphMutators`, `LayoutMutators`) at the seams. Ban `preload` of sibling-system scripts, and lint it.

### (b) Missing interface definitions programmers would have to invent

- **Types that appear in signatures but have no definition:** `ReadViews`, `WriteScope`, `ApplyContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `CompletionToken` (who constructs it, per command or pooled), `ChangeBatch`, `QueryBuffer`, `FailureSlice`, `FailureFilter`, `JoinPlan`, `WeldResult`, `BlockDescriptor` (the full field list is only in a comment), `ChangeBatch.change_keys` container type, and `LocoState`/`LocoIntent`/`LocoResult`.
- **No FAULT_CODE enumeration.** The weld path returns `OK or -FAULT_CODE`, but there is no table of codes or ownership of them.
- **`Kernel.tick_alpha` and `Kernel.step()` are referenced as globals** in the presentation example. That is an autoload singleton, which conflicts with the coding standard (dependencies injected, no static singletons for game state) and with headless testing.
  - Decide now: injected `kernel` reference through `setup(kernel)` on presentation nodes, or one explicit exception recorded in ADR-0001.
- **`submit(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, …)`** allocates a Dictionary per command and is validated as "whitelisted types, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 4 KiB" at runtime. That is fine at command rates (aim ≤ every 3 ticks). Define the validator and payload schema per command type, or each programmer invents one.
- **No interface mechanism is chosen.** GDScript has no interfaces. "Expose a clear interface" needs a rule: an `@abstract` base class (4.5+, flagged HIGH/verify, with the push_error stub as fallback) or duck-typed contracts checked by a boot-time registry lint. State which in ADR-0010.
- **Stale GDD text conflicts with the kernel.** OQ-1 is acknowledged. TR-pc-004 and TR-pc-005 still describe the physics callback and an old hook order, and the table in § Data Flow differs from TR-pc-005. Fix these before ADR-0001, or the Foundation ADR is written against a contradicted source.

### (c) Patterns and idiom concerns

1. **Weld transaction (ADR-0021): feasible, brittle.**
   - It is one WriteScope calling Graph M2 → Layout LM2 → Body BM3 → Interaction `sync_section` ×2 → assembly state. This is a plain synchronous call chain, which is easy to implement and to test headless.
   - The cost is "no rollback; first non-OK → kernel FAULTED". Correctness rests entirely on validate's `can_join` being exactly equal to what the four apply steps accept. Any drift between a `check_*` and its mutator becomes a game-ending FAULT, not a rejected command.
   - Required mitigations: a property test that, over generated section pairs, asserts that `can_join == true` implies all four mutators return OK; the verifier INV-1..INV-10 run after every weld in test builds; and a mutator-pair lint requiring each Class A mutator to have a `check_*`.
   - An alternative that needs no new engine feature: snapshot only the 4 touched blocks before apply and restore them on FAULT, instead of faulting the whole kernel. This is a design decision for technical-director, not mine.

2. **Save worker thread (ADR-0006): feasible.**
   - `Thread` plus `FileAccess` on a worker is a standard pattern when the worker receives only `PackedByteArray`s and paths, as specified.
   - The weak points are (i) `DirAccess.rename` over an existing target on Windows (marked [UNV]; spike it with a locked-file and antivirus-hold case), (ii) the "abandoned worker job" accounting (MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS 2), which needs a deterministic fake worker for tests, and (iii) a thread cannot be killed, so quit-while-writing needs a bounded join.
   - **A real number conflict:** the main-thread encode hand-off is capped at SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS 4 ms, but TR-cmd-032 allows a 32-block snapshot capture of ≤ 16.7 ms. That is above the 14.9 ms desktop frame target. The snapshot is synchronous at P6 and the only deep-copy step. Either split snapshot across frames, or accept and document one over-budget frame per autosave.

3. **Hook scheduling by `divisor/offset/after` plus topo-sort** is straightforward. It is a good fit, fully data-driven, and testable. The `tolerates_stale` rule is a good guard against hidden coupling.

4. **Dirty-key marking inside every mutator** is a discipline rule, not an enforced one, because 4.7 packed-array element writes skip setters. A missed mark is a silent presentation bug. Add a debug-build check: after each tick, hash the block and compare against "was this block's key marked dirty"; fail tests on mismatch.

5. **33 ADRs and 794 TRs for one programmer.** Three ADRs carry 64-65 primary TRs each (0006, 0007, 0024). Those will not be reviewable as single documents. Split them (container/versioning/restore-epoch; content pipeline/boot lints; filter/isolation), or write them as sectioned documents with explicit sub-decisions. Illustrative arithmetic: 794 TRs at even 0.25 day each is about 200 working days before art and content. That is a scope question for producer and creative-director, not an architecture defect. The ten Foundation ADRs and their spikes are the real gate; the rest can be written just in time.

### Lints, `src/` layout, testability

- **`src/` layout:** the sim/presentation split (`src/sim/<system>/`, `src/presentation/<system>/`, `src/kernel`, `src/save`, `src/data`, `src/debug`) is practical and matches the layering rule. Fix IC-10 (Sanity's `src/sanity/`) and keep it.
- **Lints are the weak link, and no tool is chosen.**
  - gdtoolkit's `gdlint` has no project-specific rule support, so custom rules mean a script of your own. Regex scanning covers well: `device == 0`, `Thread`/`WorkerThreadPool`/`call_deferred` in kernel code, `randi`/`randf`/`Time.get_ticks_*` in sim code, `preload` of siblings, process_priority values, and "no Node/Light2D in `src/sim/`".
  - Not regex-enforceable: "underscore-prefixed fields written only by graph_mutators.gd and three others" (TR-lsg-002), "a mutator called outside a WriteScope", and "no float on the query path". They need runtime detection (the `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` counter already exists) or a real AST pass.
  - Budget it as one tools-programmer story with a rule list in ADR-0010, run as a headless Godot script plus CI. Do not claim "lint-enforced" for rules that need an AST.
- **Warnings as errors:** the `debug/gdscript/warnings/*` project settings are set to Error and they work. Add `untyped_declaration`, `unsafe_*` and `integer_division`, and use `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")` as the architecture already says.
- **gdUnit4 headless:**
  - Strongly favourable for the sim: Scene-tree-free `RefCounted` blocks, synchronous `Kernel.step()` and an injected KernelProfile mean unit and replay tests need no scene.
  - Not covered: wall-clock budgets (editor/debug is not valid per R12; you need an exported benchmark harness with its own runner, outside gdUnit4), release-only behaviour (`assert` stripped, KRN-CTX-06), and presentation/TileMapLayer tests.
  - Pin and verify a gdUnit4 version against 4.7.2 before ADR-0010; third-party test addons lag engine releases. The CI command in the coding standards uses `--ignoreHeadlessMode`; check it on 4.7.2.
  - The `state_hash` replay-at-30/60/144 fps AC (TR-pxl-022) is the most valuable test and is cheap with this design.

### Riskiest items, in spike order

1. **S1 / SP-ENG-1: hot-path cost on a release export.** Build a stub Graph (12 phases, packed arrays), `emitter.place`, and the P3 loop with realistic entity counts. Measure accessor-call overhead and 4-tick catch-up on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. Gates ADR-0012/0014/0015/0017 and decides whether the GDExtension rung is needed.
2. **Kernel skeleton with `ctx.complete()`, hook topo-sort and WriteScope, run headless under gdUnit4.** This proves the owner-callable contract, the injected-kernel decision, token verification in release, and test-harness viability together. Gates ADR-0001/0003.
3. **S0-a/S0-b:** packed-array alias semantics, signed 64-bit literal and shift behaviour, plus H64 golden vectors. Gates ADR-0005/0010/0011.
4. **Weld transaction property test:** `can_join` vs the four mutators over generated pairs, with stub Graph/Layout/Body. Gates ADR-0021 and tells you if the no-rollback rule is survivable.
5. **Save worker spike:** `DirAccess.rename` over an existing file on Windows, locked and antivirus conditions, quit during a write, and the snapshot hitch size. Gates ADR-0006.
6. **SP-YSORT-1, pipeline step 11, lighting spike:** rendering-side, gating ADR-0008/0009/0018/0028. They are independent of the sim and can run in parallel after the first three.

### Resolve before accepting ADRs

- Define the missing types and FAULT_CODE table (b).
- Decide autoload vs injection and the interface mechanism.
- Fix OQ-1 and the stale TR-pc-004/005 text.
- Reconcile the 4 ms encode budget with the 16.7 ms snapshot cost.
- Name the lint tool and split the three oversized ADRs.

Files reviewed: `D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/architecture.md`, `D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md` (summary and spot-checks), `D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/engine-reference/godot/breaking-changes.md`, `D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/engine-reference/godot/current-best-practices.md`. No files were edited.

A note on the invocation: the call arrived with the `/tech-debt` skill text and no subcommand. I treated the LP-FEASIBILITY gate request as the task and did not run the skill.

   - If Callables, the 4.7 note is moot and the real enforcement is simpler: GDScript already rejects a typed function with a path that has no return.
   - KRN-CTX-06's "assert stripped on release" concern then reduces to one rule: the kernel must verify the returned token identity with a real `if`, never an `assert`.

5. **Cyclic typed references between systems.** The dependency diagram shows Layout and Graph depending on each other (Layout consumes Graph `instantiate_section`; Graph consumes Layout room identity). Assembly, Interaction and Body also form loops.
   - GDScript tolerates cycles through `class_name`, but `preload` cycles fail to parse.
   - Mandate `class_name` plus typed interface base classes (`GraphMutators`, `LayoutMutators`) at the seams. Ban `preload` of sibling-system scripts, and lint it.

### (b) Missing interface definitions programmers would have to invent

- **Types that appear in signatures but have no definition:** `ReadViews`, `WriteScope`, `ApplyContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `CompletionToken` (who constructs it, per command or pooled), `ChangeBatch`, `QueryBuffer`, `FailureSlice`, `FailureFilter`, `JoinPlan`, `WeldResult`, `BlockDescriptor` (the full field list is only in a comment), `ChangeBatch.change_keys` container type, and `LocoState`/`LocoIntent`/`LocoResult`.
- **No FAULT_CODE enumeration.** The weld path returns `OK or -FAULT_CODE`, but there is no table of codes or ownership of them.
- **`Kernel.tick_alpha` and `Kernel.step()` are referenced as globals** in the presentation example. That is an autoload singleton, which conflicts with the coding standard (dependencies injected, no static singletons for game state) and with headless testing.
  - Decide now: injected `kernel` reference through `setup(kernel)` on presentation nodes, or one explicit exception recorded in ADR-0001.
- **`submit(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, …)`** allocates a Dictionary per command and is validated as "whitelisted types, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 4 KiB" at runtime. That is fine at command rates (aim ≤ every 3 ticks). Define the validator and payload schema per command type, or each programmer invents one.
- **No interface mechanism is chosen.** GDScript has no interfaces. "Expose a clear interface" needs a rule: an `@abstract` base class (4.5+, flagged HIGH/verify, with the push_error stub as fallback) or duck-typed contracts checked by a boot-time registry lint. State which in ADR-0010.
- **Stale GDD text conflicts with the kernel.** OQ-1 is acknowledged. TR-pc-004 and TR-pc-005 still describe the physics callback and an old hook order, and the table in § Data Flow differs from TR-pc-005. Fix these before ADR-0001, or the Foundation ADR is written against a contradicted source.

### (c) Patterns and idiom concerns

1. **Weld transaction (ADR-0021): feasible, brittle.**
   - It is one WriteScope calling Graph M2 → Layout LM2 → Body BM3 → Interaction `sync_section` ×2 → assembly state. This is a plain synchronous call chain, which is easy to implement and to test headless.
   - The cost is "no rollback; first non-OK → kernel FAULTED". Correctness rests entirely on validate's `can_join` being exactly equal to what the four apply steps accept. Any drift between a `check_*` and its mutator becomes a game-ending FAULT, not a rejected command.
   - Required mitigations: a property test that, over generated section pairs, asserts that `can_join == true` implies all four mutators return OK; the verifier INV-1..INV-10 run after every weld in test builds; and a mutator-pair lint requiring each Class A mutator to have a `check_*`.
   - An alternative that needs no new engine feature: snapshot only the 4 touched blocks before apply and restore them on FAULT, instead of faulting the whole kernel. This is a design decision for technical-director, not mine.

2. **Save worker thread (ADR-0006): feasible.**
   - `Thread` plus `FileAccess` on a worker is a standard pattern when the worker receives only `PackedByteArray`s and paths, as specified.
   - The weak points are (i) `DirAccess.rename` over an existing target on Windows (marked [UNV]; spike it with a locked-file and antivirus-hold case), (ii) the "abandoned worker job" accounting (MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS 2), which needs a deterministic fake worker for tests, and (iii) a thread cannot be killed, so quit-while-writing needs a bounded join.
   - **A real number conflict:** the main-thread encode hand-off is capped at SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS 4 ms, but TR-cmd-032 allows a 32-block snapshot capture of ≤ 16.7 ms. That is above the 14.9 ms desktop frame target. The snapshot is synchronous at P6 and the only deep-copy step. Either split snapshot across frames, or accept and document one over-budget frame per autosave.

3. **Hook scheduling by `divisor/offset/after` plus topo-sort** is straightforward. It is a good fit, fully data-driven, and testable. The `tolerates_stale` rule is a good guard against hidden coupling.

4. **Dirty-key marking inside every mutator** is a discipline rule, not an enforced one, because 4.7 packed-array element writes skip setters. A missed mark is a silent presentation bug. Add a debug-build check: after each tick, hash the block and compare against "was this block's key marked dirty"; fail tests on mismatch.

5. **33 ADRs and 794 TRs for one programmer.** Three ADRs carry 64-65 primary TRs each (0006, 0007, 0024). Those will not be reviewable as single documents. Split them (container/versioning/restore-epoch; content pipeline/boot lints; filter/isolation), or write them as sectioned documents with explicit sub-decisions. Illustrative arithmetic: 794 TRs at even 0.25 day each is about 200 working days before art and content. That is a scope question for producer and creative-director, not an architecture defect. The ten Foundation ADRs and their spikes are the real gate; the rest can be written just in time.

### Lints, `src/` layout, testability

- **`src/` layout:** the sim/presentation split (`src/sim/<system>/`, `src/presentation/<system>/`, `src/kernel`, `src/save`, `src/data`, `src/debug`) is practical and matches the layering rule. Fix IC-10 (Sanity's `src/sanity/`) and keep it.
- **Lints are the weak link, and no tool is chosen.**
  - gdtoolkit's `gdlint` has no project-specific rule support, so custom rules mean a script of your own. Regex scanning covers well: `device == 0`, `Thread`/`WorkerThreadPool`/`call_deferred` in kernel code, `randi`/`randf`/`Time.get_ticks_*` in sim code, `preload` of siblings, process_priority values, and "no Node/Light2D in `src/sim/`".
  - Not regex-enforceable: "underscore-prefixed fields written only by graph_mutators.gd and three others" (TR-lsg-002), "a mutator called outside a WriteScope", and "no float on the query path". They need runtime detection (the `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` counter already exists) or a real AST pass.
  - Budget it as one tools-programmer story with a rule list in ADR-0010, run as a headless Godot script plus CI. Do not claim "lint-enforced" for rules that need an AST.
- **Warnings as errors:** the `debug/gdscript/warnings/*` project settings are set to Error and they work. Add `untyped_declaration`, `unsafe_*` and `integer_division`, and use `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")` as the architecture already says.
- **gdUnit4 headless:**
  - Strongly favourable for the sim: Scene-tree-free `RefCounted` blocks, synchronous `Kernel.step()` and an injected KernelProfile mean unit and replay tests need no scene.
  - Not covered: wall-clock budgets (editor/debug is not valid per R12; you need an exported benchmark harness with its own runner, outside gdUnit4), release-only behaviour (`assert` stripped, KRN-CTX-06), and presentation/TileMapLayer tests.
  - Pin and verify a gdUnit4 version against 4.7.2 before ADR-0010; third-party test addons lag engine releases. The CI command in the coding standards uses `--ignoreHeadlessMode`; check it on 4.7.2.
  - The `state_hash` replay-at-30/60/144 fps AC (TR-pxl-022) is the most valuable test and is cheap with this design.
